label: Northwest Indiana x Personal Injury
source: A region rather than a city, and the offices are the reason. Valparaiso holds eight of these firms' offices, Merrillville six, Portage three and Crown Point two, across Lake and Porter counties, and no town dominates. Naming one of them as the market would put a Merrillville firm in a Valparaiso ranking, which is the mistake this directory already corrected in Maryland, and splitting the market in two would produce two rankings of seven firms each, which is the mistake it already corrected in Baltimore and Lakeland. Somebody hurt in Portage would genuinely consider a firm in Merrillville twenty miles away, so one regional market is the honest comparison set. Candidates from Google Places across Portage, Valparaiso, Merrillville, Hammond, Gary and Crown Point (scripts/discover_places.py, 83 domains), kept only where the firm's own site publishes an injury practice page and it holds an office in postal area 463xx or 464xx. No Ahrefs metrics, so D2 scores pending for every firm here.

unresolved_notes.forthepeople.com: Excluded from every cohort. Morgan & Morgan holds an office here and in roughly a thousand other markets, and a profile on this site asserts one home market.
unresolved_notes.wewin.com: Isaacs & Isaacs. Its own structured data says the firm is headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky and runs thirteen offices across Kentucky, Indiana and Ohio, and the injury practice page our check found is a Lexington, Kentucky page. A firm's market is where it is based, so this one belongs to a market this directory does not cover, whatever its Valparaiso and Griffith listings say.
unresolved_notes.allen.law: Held back, not excluded. The Indiana discipline index identifies the firm's founder as the respondent in In the Matter of Kenneth J. Allen, decided 13 September 2002 by the Supreme Court of Indiana (https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/853098/in-the-matter-of-kenneth-j-allen/). Indiana prints the respondent's full name in the case name, which is the strong identification path, and the decision's text contains the words public reprimand, suspension and Valparaiso, which is this firm's city. That is enough to stop and not enough to publish: whether the court imposed a reprimand, imposed a suspension or refused both is the difference between two very different sentences about a named person, and nobody here has read the order. A person reads it before this profile goes up, the same rule that is holding Brandon J. Broderick back in New York.
